_comment: Which unsatisfied trace obligations are known boundaries rather than gaps.
A boundary is a place where the analyzed source stops on purpose and the
behavior past it follows from declared evidence: a runtime-generated
implementation, a profile-selected alternative, a transaction the caller or
container completes, a documented library or platform API, or an HTTP call
answered by an endpoint anchored in this repository. Everything not listed
here stays a gap. A boundary never changes a trace's resolution; it only
decides whether the trace is bounded or incomplete.
diagnostic_codes: adapter diagnostic codes attached to the obligation's edge.
An obligation is a boundary only when every code on its edge is listed.
obligation_codes: trace obligation reason codes that are boundaries by themselves.
library_codes: codes an adapter emits for a call that leaves the source; the
call is a boundary only when its provider is listed under known_libraries for
the calling language. An unknown provider stays a gap.
known_libraries: per language. 'prefixes' match qualified type providers
(type:java.util.List), 'modules' match imported modules exactly or by a
'/' subpath (module:react, module:react-dom/client), and 'ambient' accepts the
names the language registry binds without declaration (global:console).
A provider may list candidates separated by '|' (type:java.util.X|jakarta.persistence.X);
it is known only when every candidate is.

assumptions.generated_implementation: The generated implementation behaves as its declaration specifies. {reason}
assumptions.config_selected: The active configuration selects one of the listed alternatives. {reason}
assumptions.transaction_completion: The caller or container completes the transaction. {reason}
assumptions.library_call: {provider} behaves as its published API documents. {reason}
assumptions.endpoint_in_repo: The request reaches the endpoint anchored in this repository. {reason}
